subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: The Silk Road
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Silk Road usable.

hook.text: Chinese silk reached Rome 2,000 years ago—across deserts, mountains, and bandit territory.

buildup.text: The Silk Road was a network of trade routes connecting Asia to Europe, spanning over 6,000 km.

discovery.text: Goods moved through relay—each merchant covered a segment, passing items to the next trader.

twist.text: Most traders never traveled the whole route. The system worked because of trusted handoffs.

climax.text: The Silk Road didn't just move goods. It spread ideas, religions, and diseases between empires.

punchline.text: The first global supply chain ran on camels and trust.

quiz.question: How did goods move along the Silk Road?
options: One merchant traveled the whole route
